title: Suspense boundaries stream in as data loads

slides.text: Don't let slow data block the whole page 🐢
slides.say: Imagine a profile page where the posts take a while to load. You don't want the whole page to wait.
Wrap Posts in a Suspense boundary. This tells React to start streaming the HTML before Posts has its data.

slides.text: Content is revealed before any script loads.
slides.say: React first sends the layout, the cover, and the glimmer fallback.

steps.say: Later, the posts finish loading on the server.
React sends the rest of the HTML, plus a small inline script tag.
That script swaps the glimmer for the posts. This happens even before React itself has loaded in the browser.

slides.text: Only Suspense-enabled data, like a Promise read with use, suspends. Data fetched in an Effect or event handler isn't detected.
slides.say: One catch: only Suspense enabled data, like a promise read with use, can suspend. Data fetched in an effect or an event handler isn't detected.
